correctness.rationale: Scale invariance reduces to unit Weibull scale. Writing the Weibull variable as exp(Y/k) with exp(Y) exponential gives an exact representation. The log-Gamma expansion through cubic order yields the mean and variance expansions, and direct logarithmic expansion of the moving one-standard-deviation endpoints produces equal inward first-order endpoint shifts of magnitude zeta(3)/(a k). Taylor expansion of the smooth reflected-Gumbel CDF then gives the displayed coefficient and an O(k^{-2}) remainder. Positivity is explicit. The standalone verifier independently recomputes exact finite-k probabilities but is not used to establish the asymptotic theorem.

originality.rationale: The motivating full text proves the Weibull inequality only for 0<k<=1 and records failure at k=3 with a finite plot for 1<=k<=10. Although the same paper gives the Gumbel one-sigma mass, it does not state that large-shape standardized Weibull laws approach its reflection at this functional, nor a first-order 1/k term or the zeta(3) coefficient. Eight candidate-specific published-record searches and own-ledger comparisons found no covering claim.
residual_risks: The logarithmic Weibull-to-Gumbel relation and Gamma-function moment expansions are classical, so an equivalent first-order expansion may exist in older reliability or extreme-value literature under terminology not retrieved by the searches.
The theorem proves eventual recovery above the Gaussian benchmark but does not locate the optimal finite recovery threshold or prove a unique benchmark crossing.

value.rationale: The source explicitly exhibits failure of the Gaussian one-sigma comparison for Weibull shape k=3, so the behavior beyond the infinitely divisible range is a motivated structural gap. The new result resolves the far-right endpoint: it identifies the reflected-Gumbel limit, proves approach from below, supplies the exact Apéry-constant correction, and therefore establishes eventual recovery above the Gaussian benchmark. This is a signed endpoint law for the source's central functional rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
